```java 
import org.junit.*;
import static org.junit.Assert.*; // for Assertions in JUnit v4 and later versions (assertEquals) is imported automatically from junit package  
    
public class TypeCheckerTest {    public void testIsStringType() {         assertTrue(isStringType(Class.class));          System.out.println("1");        notTrue(isStringType((Integer).class));           // Expected output: true -> False, so 'assertFalse' is used
                                                                     assertEquals('Expected false', !true);                    }  @Test public void testRef() {         RefType ref = new RefType();          assertNotNull("Reference should not be null", v(String.class));           // Expected output: true -> False, so 'assertFalse' is used
                                                                     assertEquals('Expected reference equality', type == t);  } @Test public void testProgram() {         boolean result = IsStringType((Class) RefType());          assertTrue("Is String Type should return True",result );           // Expected output: true -> False, so 'assertFalse' is used
                                                                     assertEquals('Expected false', !true);                    }   }; ``` C# Unit Tests are the same as Java. Here they test methods in your Program class and their expected results using JUnit from NUnit framework for .NET (CSharp) code: 
```csharp    public void IsStringTypeTest()     {        Type t = typeof(string);         bool result  = CodeSnippetRunner.Program.IsStringType((int )t );          Assert.True("Expected true, got " + !result , ref  == v (typeof')); } ```
Please note that JUnit 5 is the recommended way to write tests in Java since it's more maintainable and readable than previous versions of junit framework like junit4/junit3 for .NET. You should use assert statements instead of assertEquals, as they provide better visibility into what your test code does if something goes wrong (useful when you want a debug-message).
